content.title: About
content.content: Soft pretzels filled with cheese are a baked snack made from yeasted dough, brushed with a golden crust and stuffed with melted cheese. They have a tender flavor, a slightly salty aroma, and a gooey cheese center.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cheese‑filled soft pretzels are a popular bar and café snack in the United States.
The traditional German "Brezel" has a hard crust; the soft version emerged in the early 20th century in the US.
Cheese fillings often include cheddar, mozzarella, or a blend of several cheeses.
In some regions they are served with mustard or honey dipping sauces.
Spiced versions add paprika, garlic, or other seasonings to the dough.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: The cheese filling provides both dairy and plant protein, supporting tissue repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Yeast‑leavened dough is rich in B1, B2, and B6 vitamins, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: Soft pretzels deliver fast‑acting carbohydrates for an energy boost.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used, the pretzel contains more fiber, beneficial for digestion.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: The cheese filling can trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or dairy protein allergy.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salt used in the dough and filling may be a concern for those monitoring sodium intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese‑filled soft pretzels are relatively calorie‑dense, so they should be eaten in moderation.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The dough contains wheat, making the product unsuitable for individuals with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, sliced and paired with mustard, cheese sauce, or a tomato dip. They also work well as a base for mini sandwiches or appetizer bites.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soft pretzels in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer shelf life keep them refrigerated – up to a week – or freeze and reheat in the oven before serving.
